entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Siege of Yorktown was a pivotal event in the American Revolutionary War, marking a decisive victory for American and French forces against the British Army in October 1781. This siege, led by General George Washington and the Comte de Rochambeau, lasted from September 28 to October 19, 1781, and ended with the surrender of British General Charles Cornwallis, effectively ending the war and paving the way for American independence.

The siege was a result of a series of strategic maneuvers and battles, including the Battle of Yorktown and the Battle of the Chesapeake, which weakened the British position and created a sense of urgency among the British commanders. The French fleet's arrival in the Chesapeake Bay in September 1781 further isolated the British forces and set the stage for the final assault.

The consequences of the Siege of Yorktown were far-reaching, leading to the signing of the Treaty of Paris in 1783, which formally ended the American Revolutionary War and recognized American independence. This victory marked a significant turning point in world history, as it not only shaped the course of American history but also had a lasting impact on the global balance of power.

As General Washington noted, 'The bravery and perseverance of our troops have been truly heroic,' and the siege remains a testament to the power of cooperation and determination in the face of adversity.
